DLSS5 source and binary follow-up — 16 October 2026

CONCLUSION
There is now strong, specific evidence that our tests execute NVIDIA's leaked
DLSS5 neural model through a community hardware-compatibility implementation.
The working library is not an unmodified, NVIDIA-supported RTX3090 release.
However, its failed whole-file signature is explained by identifiable GPU
compatibility modifications; it is not evidence that the model is a grading
filter or that the NVIDIA model weights were replaced.

WHAT THE SOURCE DOES
The audited BlenDLSS bridge at commit b4a62f77ef2de2cbc610be7fee344d1c0854b241
loads NVSDK_NGX_D3D12_Init_Ext, CreateFeature, EvaluateFeature and ReleaseFeature
from the selected nvngx_dlssnr.dll. It creates Feature 18. Each evaluation is
given GPU colour, depth and motion textures, temporal reset state, dimensions
and the DLSSNR intensity, structure, tone and style controls. It waits for GPU
completion and reads the resulting output texture back.

Our Python native_backend.py calls that bridge directly. It does not import
the upstream cpu_preview.py fallback. C10/C11 failures raise exceptions rather
than switch to a CPU approximation. There is no added colour grade, sharpening
or beauty filter in the delivered native image path. Flipping image orientation,
restoring opaque alpha and discarding the extra indicator padding are wrapper
operations. The comparison video separately adds labels and a divider.

SOURCE DOES NOT EQUAL COMPLETE CORE SOURCE
The NVIDIA network/inference implementation is proprietary compiled code.
Reading the wrapper alone cannot prove its internal math. The binary comparison
below provides independent evidence about what the working runtime contains.

BINARY COMPARISON AGAINST THE NVIDIA-SIGNED COPY
Both runtime files identify as 310.8.0.0 and contain 165840496 bytes.
Signed comparison file SHA256:
e16bcf15e16e13f527491cdf7845b2fe6521a738d8f7c9c721866a8496e1fc8e
Working community file SHA256:
dcc0dc2414aedec4a8e084647070383be068554042587180c20c784d4772d36f

1. The WEIGHTS_HT resource is IDENTICAL, byte for byte: 147695410 bytes.
   Weight-resource SHA256 in both:
   836f445d06ecd2e59bb9f17b84b91c143396fd76ccda1c9dc7fe81d5edd548f4
   Its contents include named network layers, e.g. block0.layer0.layer.

2. The entire .rsrc resource section and .rdata section are identical.

3. Exactly 19 bytes differ in host .text machine code. Disassembly locates
   these changes at architecture requirements/dispatch checks. The minimum
   architecture constant changes from 0x1b0 to 0x170; three older-architecture
   branches skip the unsupported-architecture path. No other host-code byte
   differs from the signed copy.

4. The other 15310900 changed bytes are entirely within the 15 original CUDA
   fat-binary containers. The signed containers have SM120 code. The working
   containers provide compressed CUDA binaries declaring targets 75, 86, 89
   and 120. Decompression produces valid NVIDIA CUDA ELF objects.

5. In ALL 15 containers, the decompressed SM120 binary is IDENTICAL to the
   signed original. All 15 also contain the added architecture-86 binary for
   Ampere-family execution. This explains why a scan for uncompressed ELF
   magic found none in the working file: its objects are compressed.

6. There are ZERO changed bytes outside these GPU containers and the 19
   host-code architecture edits. File sizes and all resource hashes agree.

These checks establish substantially more than matching a product-name string
or seeing a successful API return. They explain the invalid signature while
showing that the signed NVIDIA weight resource and original SM120 code remain.

WHAT REMAINS UNPROVEN
The added architecture-86 GPU binaries are not bit-identical to architecture-
120 binaries and cannot be expected to have identical machine instructions.
Their numerical equivalence has not been tested against supported hardware.
The complete proprietary inference graph has not been reimplemented/audited.
Our controls, colour conventions and integration have not been certified by
NVIDIA. This leaked model need not match the revision, tuning or content shown
in a particular online demonstration. Static source review also does not prove
the downloaded bridge binary was reproducibly built from that exact source.

Accordingly, the defensible description is:
"NVIDIA DLSS5 model weights, executed through an unofficial GPU compatibility
runtime and Blender bridge; official numerical/visual equivalence unverified."

The car's subtle result is an observation of this setup. It does not prove
that DLSS5 only performs grading or establish its maximum possible improvement.
Neither a failed publisher signature nor leaked distribution alone settles
those questions. A known-image reference test would be the next useful
functional comparison, rather than further arbitrary slider increases.
